ahead: CANDIDATE_ENERGY.md's Energy(N) equals E_corr(N) exactly (a Haar/martingale block-average telescoping identity, proved by orthogonal-projection algebra alone, no arithmetic input). It satisfies every Section 8 constraint (mean/central mode, cross terms between scales computed and proved exactly zero, changing q/chi/beta, sharp endpoint, no primes-only replacement) and results_s8_candidate_energy.json confirms it to floating-point precision at N in {2000,5000,10000,30000,100000}. But being an exact identity it carries zero arithmetic content and gives no progress toward E_corr(N) << N^{2+eps}: it only reorganizes the same number into dyadic block-length pieces. The next real step is not more scale bookkeeping; it is proving decay for the per-scale pieces Delta_k(N) themselves (Section 3-4 of CANDIDATE_ENERGY.md), which numerically look roughly geometric (finest scale ~50% of the total, each octave up roughly halving) but that pattern is only measured at 5 values of N, not proved, and proving it would require real arithmetic input (something like the LOCALIZED_MIXED_ENERGY.md route's unresolved eq 20/eq 22, which this document explicitly does not touch or shorten). No exceptional zero is known to exist, so all five numerical rows have C_N=0 and E_corr(N)=E(N); the identity is stated and proved for general C_N (Section 1, Section 6) and would need no change if a concrete exceptional q,chi,beta were later assumed.

work.what: In hunts/prime_pair_error/CANDIDATE_ENERGY.md, Section 2 defines, for the corrected prime-pair residual x_h = r_N(h) - C_N(h) (1<=h<=N, from CORRECTED_RH_BRIDGE.md eq 1), padded by zeros to length M=2^K (K=ceil(log2 N)), the dyadic block-average orthogonal projections P_k (average over contiguous blocks of length 2^k) and detail energies Delta_k(N) = ||P_k x - P_{k+1} x||_2^2 for k=0..K-1, plus the mean term M*mu(N)^2 where mu(N) is the global average of x. Section 3 proves the exact identity E_corr(N) = 2*M*mu(N)^2 + 2*sum_{k=0}^{K-1} Delta_k(N) unconditionally, by elementary orthogonal-projection algebra (no arithmetic input). Section 4's numerics (from hunts/prime_pair_error/results_s8_candidate_energy.json, produced by hunts/prime_pair_error/s8_candidate_energy.py) show, at N in {2000,5000,10000,30000,100000} with no known exceptional zero (so C_N=0 and x_h=r_N(h)=the original CHHL residual e(N,h)), that the finest scale (block length 1) carries about 50% of E_corr(N), and each successive octave of block length carries roughly half of what the previous octave carried, down to a noisy tail of coarse scales each under 1%. This is only measured at five values of N, not proved. The task: determine whether Delta_k(N) can be proved unconditionally to decay geometrically in k (e.g. Delta_k(N) << 2^{-k} E_corr(N), or any other explicit rate) for a genuine range of k, or find that no such decay is provable and say precisely what blocks it (e.g. it would require controlling correlations of r_N(h) - C_N(h) across shifts, which is exactly the kind of estimate LOCALIZED_MIXED_ENERGY.md's Section 5 (its eq 20) and Section 6 (its eq 22 cross terms) already tried and left open). A proved decay rate would let the identity in CANDIDATE_ENERGY.md Section 3 do real work: reducing the E_corr(N) << N^{2+eps} target to bounding the finitely many largest-share scales instead of the whole sum at once. Numerical experimentation at larger N (the script hunts/prime_pair_error/s8_candidate_energy.py already computes this for arbitrary N, reusing hunts/prime_pair_error/probe.py's von_mangoldt/singular_series/psi2_fft) is a reasonable way to get more evidence on the decay rate and its uniformity in N before attempting a proof.

edges.why: w-scale-decay-proof needs the exact multiscale identity and per-scale definitions of CANDIDATE_ENERGY.md, which this attempt (w-s8-candidate-energy) produced; there is nothing to bound a decay rate on until that decomposition exists.
